# How to Remove Personal Details From a Document Before Sharing It With an AI Tool

> **In short:** You can keep the helpful content of a document and hide the personal details by replacing names, account numbers and addresses with neutral placeholders like "Person One." Always check the result yourself, because a missed detail stays visible to the chatbot.

Many people paste a letter, bill or work file into an AI chatbot and ask for a summary or a rewrite. That can be very useful, but the document often contains details you would not want to share: names, phone numbers, account numbers, home addresses. In this guide you will make a safe working copy, build a short list of what to hide, swap in placeholders, and check the result before anything leaves your computer. By the end, you will have a version the chatbot can work with and a clear way to put the real details back yourself.

## Before you start

- **A document you want help with**, saved on your computer or in a cloud service such as Google Docs or Microsoft Word.
- **Any AI chatbot account** you already use, or a free one. Placeholders work the same way in every tool.
- **A blank notes file** (Notepad, Notes, or any text app) for your private list. It must stay on your device and never go into the chatbot.
- **About 15 to 20 minutes.** Longer documents take more time to check.

## Step 1 — Make a working copy of the document

Never edit your original. Open the document and save a second copy first. In Word, look for **Save As** under the File menu. In Google Docs, look for **Make a copy** under the File menu. If you cannot find either, look for a "Duplicate" option in your file manager, or right-click the file and choose Copy, then paste it back into the same folder.

Name the copy something clear, such as "bill-for-chatbot." Once it is open, you should see the same text and layout as the original, with the file name changed at the top or in the title bar.

💬 Example: Give the copy a plain name like "letter-working-copy" so you never confuse it with the file that holds the real details.

You'll know it worked when you have two files side by side, and the one you are editing has the new name.

## Step 2 — Make a private list of what to hide

Read the document once from top to bottom. Every time you see something that identifies a person, an account or a place, write it in your notes file. Include full names, first names used alone, email addresses, phone numbers, street addresses, account or policy numbers, dates of birth, and ID numbers. Do not forget the small things, like a company name that is unique to one employer, or a school your child attends.

Give each item a simple label in your list, such as "Person One = Maria Lopez" or "Account A = 4478-2219." This list is the key that lets you put everything back later, so keep it on your device.

If your document is long, go one page at a time and tick off each page as you finish it. If you are not sure whether something is personal, add it to the list anyway. Extra caution costs you nothing.

💬 Example: Write in your notes: "Person One = Maria Lopez, Account A = [your account number here]."

You'll know it worked when your list covers every name, number and address you noticed on the first read-through.

## Step 3 — Replace each detail with a placeholder

Open the search tool in your working copy. Look for **Find and replace**, often under an Edit menu or behind a magnifying-glass icon near the top. Keyboard shortcuts vary by program, so the menu is the safer route if you are unsure.

In the "Find" box, type the first item from your list exactly as it appears in the document. In the "Replace" box, type its placeholder. Then choose **Replace all**. Repeat for each item on your list. Use placeholders that are obviously fake, such as "Person One," "Account A" or "123 Sample Street," so you can spot them later.

Be consistent. If "Maria" and "Maria Lopez" both appear, replace both. If you are not sure the program will catch every version, search for each spelling separately.

💬 Example: In the Find box, type "Maria Lopez"; in the Replace box, type "Person One"; then choose Replace all.

You'll know it worked when the original name no longer appears in your search results, and the placeholder appears wherever the name used to be.

## Step 4 — Check the hidden corners

Replacing text in the main body is not always enough. Many documents hide personal details in places you do not see on the page. Look for headers and footers at the top and bottom of each page; they often carry a name, a phone number or a file path. Look for comments and tracked changes, which show the people who edited the file. Look for a signature block at the end of a letter, and for a logo or image that contains text.

To check document details, look for an option called **Properties** or **Document info** under the File menu. Author names and company names are often stored there. You can clear them or leave them blank.

Also rename the file itself, because the file name is often the first thing an AI tool sees.

💬 Example: Rename your file from "Maria-Lopez-bill-March" to "bill-working-copy" before you upload it anywhere.

You'll know it worked when you have scrolled through every header, footer and comment and none of them show a real name or number.

## Step 5 — Read the result yourself

Now read the cleaned document from start to finish, slowly. Ask yourself whether anyone could identify the person, the account or the place from what remains. Watch for clues that are not names: a unique job title, a rare street, a school mascot, a specific date of birth, or a story only one family would recognize. If a clue could identify someone, replace it with a general description, such as "a local school."

For a final check, use the search tool once more. Search for each original item on your list and confirm zero results. Then search for the at sign (@) and for long strings of digits. Any hits deserve a second look.

Remember that a tool cannot guarantee anonymity. It can only help you hide what you can see, so your own reading is the real safety step.

💬 Example: After cleaning, check the final version for the phrase "the only pediatric clinic in" and replace it with "a local clinic" if it appears.

You'll know it worked when a search for each original detail returns nothing, and a stranger reading the page could not tell who it describes.

## Step 6 — Share the cleaned copy and bring the details back yourself

Open your AI chatbot, start a new conversation, and paste in the cleaned text, or upload the cleaned file if the tool offers an upload button. Ask your question in plain words. The chatbot's answer will use the placeholders, so it will still work for summarizing, rewriting or explaining the document.

Before you paste, look in the tool's settings or help pages for privacy or data-control options. Each company describes how it handles conversations in its own words, and it is worth reading those explanations once. Keep in mind that a chatbot can make mistakes, so check any important answer against your original file.

When the answer comes back, use your private list to put the real names and numbers back yourself, in your own copy. The AI never needs to see them.

💬 Example: "Here is a cleaned-up letter where names and numbers are replaced with placeholders like Person One. Summarize the main points in [number] short bullet points."

You'll know it worked when the chatbot's answer makes sense using the placeholders, and you can match each one back to your private list.

## Common mistakes

- **Forgetting headers, footers, comments and file names.** These often hold the same personal details as the body text. Fix it by checking every page edge and the file name in Step 4.
- **Replacing only the first spelling.** If a name appears as "Maria," "M. Lopez" and "Maria Lopez," a single search misses two of them. Fix it by searching for each version separately, then searching once more to confirm.
- **Keeping your private list in the chat.** If you paste the key into the chatbot, you have undone the whole process. Fix it by keeping the list in a notes file on your device only, and never copying it into a prompt.

## What this means for you

- **In everyday life:** Before you ask a chatbot to explain a medical bill, a lease or a school letter, swap the names and numbers for placeholders first. You still get a clear explanation, and your family's details stay with you.
- **For your business or work:** Before sharing a customer list, a contract draft or an internal report with an AI tool, follow the same steps and check your company's own rules about which tools are approved. Those rules come from your employer, not from this guide.
- **If you're just getting started:** Begin with a short, non-sensitive document, such as a recipe with a family name in it, and practice the find-and-replace steps until they feel routine.

## Try it now

Pick one document on your computer that has a name or number in it. Make a working copy, write down three personal details in your notes file, and replace them with placeholders. Then read the first paragraph once more and check that nothing real remains. That is the whole habit, and it takes about two minutes.
